propositions: Repository-wide documentation lacks centralized governance policy defining audience matrix, lifecycle, canonical sources, citation rules, and historical correction procedures, requiring formalization in docs/documentation-policy.md.

Maintained prose across markdown, help text, metadata, and embedded descriptions violates stated punctuation, diction, formality, and paragraph rules, necessitating source-aware compliance checking and authoring-time validation.

External documentation contains false guidance on operation certificates, import idempotency, CLI options, configuration scope, identity verification, and Jira setup that conflicts with current implementation and can cause incorrect operation.

Internal architecture, event schema, concurrency, migration, and ADR documentation does not reflect current implementation state or subsystem boundaries, requiring rewrite from actual code and configuration.

Developer comments, docstrings, and executable prose lack consistent policy for contextual necessity, historical preservation, ticket citations, and removal of ornamental or duplicated content, requiring inventory, classification, and format-aware validation.

Generated artifacts including configuration reference, ADR index, CLI reference, and MCP descriptions lack recorded ownership, canonical sources, and drift detection, requiring typed ownership registry and generator-local descriptor protocol.
